correctness.rationale: On the 81 points by 108 lines incidence matrix N, NN^T=4I+A_{H(4,3)} has exact eigenvalues 12,9,6,3,0 with multiplicities 1,8,24,32,16. The biregular Laplacian has orthogonal disjoint-support eigenspaces ker N^T of dimension 16 at eigenvalue 4 and ker N of dimension 43 at eigenvalue 3, requiring 16 point and 43 line inputs. The extracted standalone checker builds all integer entries and verifies rank N=65 and modular observation ranks 16,32,24,8,1 for the relevant rational spectral projectors with prime 101; the known eigenspace dimensions turn these into exact rational rank equalities. The 65 unactuated line columns are independent. For each positive singular eigenvalue, the Laplacian eigenvector observation differs only by a nonzero scalar multiplier in the line coordinates. PBH proves controllability with 59 and the lower bound proves optimality. A zero-forcing test finds no available initial forcing move.

originality.rationale: The identified exact 189-vertex dedicated coordinate actuator invariant and explicit non-zero-forcing optimum are not asserted in any inspected accessible source. The 2011 zero-forcing sufficiency theorem does not imply controllability for this stalled placement; the 2013 maximum-multiplicity result treats unrestricted input matrices and only yields 43 here; earlier ordinary Gray graph (54 vertices) zero-forcing results have different degree and eigenspace structure. Preexisting counterexamples to dedicated multiplicity equality, including a previously recorded weighted-hypercube family, are credited rather than claimed anew. Publication priority remains uncertain because the full 2014 Gray thesis and all specialist work could not be exhaustively inspected.
residual_risks: The restricted-access 2014 Gray-graph thesis was inspected only at the abstract level, and might have unobserved extended results.
Specialized or unindexed 4D incidence-network leader-selection literature could predate the result.
Absence of an indexed exact number is not proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: This exact invariant concerns the first natural higher-dimensional Gray point-line incidence construction, which becomes biregular. Its two distinct support-separated kernel eigenspaces enforce an additive budget of 16+43=59, a substantial 16-input gap over its largest eigenvalue multiplicity 43. An explicit minimum placement is verified and is not zero forcing. This provides a relevant and reproducible fixed-network benchmark for leader selection, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. No infinite-family theorem is claimed.
